meta.title: Promoted Housing in Uruguay: what it is and what it means for you
meta.h1: Promoted housing: what Law 18.795 is and what changes if you buy or rent
meta.description: What promoted housing in Uruguay (Law 18.795) is: benefits for the investor, exemption from ITP on the first sale, what to ask as a buyer or tenant and where to verify it at the ANV.
meta.answer: Promoted housing is the one that is built or recycled under Law 18.795, which gives tax benefits to investors who create social interest housing, either to sell or to rent. The projects are declared promoted by the Executive Power together with the Agencia Nacional de Vivienda (ANV). For you, as a buyer or tenant, it can mean a more competitive price, possible exemption from ITP on the first purchase and, for rentals, a higher cap in the Rental Guarantee Fund. Before buying, confirm with the ANV and with your escribano (notary) what benefits and conditions that project has.

sections.h2: What it is, in simple terms
paras: Law 18.795 of 2011 declared it a national interest to improve access to social housing. For that it allows tax benefits for construction, renovation, expansion or recycling projects of homes, both for sale and for rent. According to the ANV, the law "grants tax benefits to investors".

Therefore, when you see a new building in Montevideo advertised as "promoted housing", it means the developer accessed that regime. It is not a state housing plan nor a cooperative: it is a private investment with fiscal incentives.
Article 4 of the law authorizes the Executive Power to grant, among others, these benefits to promoted projects:
bullets: Exemption from income tax generated by the promoted activity.
Exemption from the Property Tax on those properties.
Exemption from VAT on the sale, construction, renovation, expansion and recycling of the homes.
Exemption from ITP for the seller, the buyer or both, in the first transfer of the home.
sections.tip: A project being promoted does not guarantee that all those benefits will reach you as a buyer. Ask in writing which one applies to your purchase, especially the ITP exemption.

sections.h2: If you buy a promoted home
paras: What will most affect you is the ITP: in a regular sale, according to the DGI, the buyer pays 2% of the real cadastral value. If the first sale of a promoted home is exempt for the buyer, you save that cost. But it only applies to the first transfer: if you later sell it, the next buyer pays the normal ITP.

Also, many promoted projects are sold off-plan. Therefore the same precautions as any construction purchase apply: registered purchase promise, investigate the developer and understand the adjustment of the installments.

A significant part of promoted homes is bought for renting. The regime may include benefits for those who rent a promoted home, but they depend on the project’s conditions and the regulations in force at the time of the declaration. Do not assume benefits without confirming them with an accountant and the ANV.

sections.h2: If you rent a promoted home
paras: For the tenant, the most concrete difference is in the guarantees: according to the ANV, the Rental Guarantee Fund allows a slightly higher maximum rent amount when it is a promoted home. If you have that guarantee, ask in the listing whether the apartment is promoted.
Otherwise, the contract and the tenant’s rights are the same as in any rental.

sections.h2: How to verify that a project is promoted
steps: Ask the developer for the declaration number or resolution of the project.
Check the ANV promoted housing website, which publishes project and price information.
Ask your escribano (notary) to confirm which exemptions apply to your purchase.
If you are going to rent it, consult an accountant about income taxes.

paras: The regime has been used a lot in intermediate and central neighborhoods of Montevideo, and there are also projects in other departments such as Canelones and Maldonado. The conditions have changed over the years according to the areas the State wanted to promote. Therefore it is not enough that it "is promoted": the period and the rules under which it was declared matter.

bullets: Is the project declared promoted? What is the resolution?
Which benefit applies to me as a buyer? Is the ITP exempt in my purchase?
Are there any usage or resale conditions for the unit?
What is the estimated delivery date and the escritura?
What are the estimated common expenses once the building is completed?
Is the price in dollars or UI, and how are the installments adjusted?

paras: Compare the price of a promoted unit with used apartments in the same area, adding common expenses and the tax savings that actually apply to you. On Casa-Libre you can see apartments for sale and rent in Montevideo on the map and write directly via WhatsApp, also from the iPhone and Android apps.

faq.q: Can I rent a promoted house with the MVOT guarantee?
faq.a: Yes, if you meet the requirements of the Rental Guarantee Fund. According to the ANV, the maximum guaranteed rent amount is slightly higher when the house is promoted.
A house built or recycled under Law 18.795, which gives tax benefits to investors who create social interest housing to sell or rent.

faq.q: Is ITP paid when buying a promoted house?
faq.a: The law allows exemption from ITP on the first transfer, to the seller, to the buyer or to both. Confirm with your escribano if it applies to your purchase.
It can have competitive prices because of the developer's tax benefits, but not always. Compare with used properties in the same area.

faq.q: Where can I check if a project is promoted?
faq.a: At the Agencia Nacional de Vivienda (ANV), which manages the regime and publishes project information.
